about: InterCat's HTTP/1.1 head decoder at version 1 (contracts/decoders-v1.md §4): each case a whole request or response head as WinINet's capture keeps one, its bytes one character each, U+0000 to U+00FF, and the decoding version 1 makes of it - the bytes it read, each field with the first and last bytes it came from and its value, what it did not decode, and whether it reached the empty line that ends a head. A decoder that decodes any case otherwise is another version, with a corpus of its own (§3a).

cases.name: a request line, a Host field and the empty line
cases.head: request

cases.name: a status line with its reason, and a length
cases.head: response

cases.name: a status line whose reason is empty
cases.head: response

cases.name: a status line with no reason and no space before it
cases.head: response

cases.name: an HTTP/1.0 status line, and a reason of three words
cases.head: response
cases.bytes:
HTTP/1.0 404 Not Found Here
Server: x

cases.name: lines ended by LF alone
cases.head: request

cases.name: a value between optional spaces and tabs
cases.head: request

cases.name: an empty value
cases.head: request

cases.name: an absolute target with a query
cases.head: request

cases.name: a value's bytes outside visible ASCII
cases.head: request

cases.name: bytes after the empty line
cases.head: request
cases.notDecoded: 4 bytes follow the empty line that ends the head; a head holds none, so they are not decoded.

cases.name: a line continuing the one before it
cases.head: request
cases.bytes:
GET / HTTP/1.1
X-A: 1
  continued
Host: a
cases.notDecoded: Line 3, from byte 24, begins with whitespace, continuing the line before it as HTTP/1.1 no longer allows, so the head is not decoded from it on.

cases.name: a line holding no colon
cases.head: request
cases.notDecoded: Line 2, from byte 16, holds no colon, so it is not a field line, and the head is not decoded from it on.

cases.name: whitespace before a colon
cases.head: request
cases.notDecoded: Line 2, from byte 16, names its field with nothing, or with a character a field name cannot hold - whitespace before its colon is one - so the head is not decoded from it on.

cases.name: a field named with nothing
cases.head: request
cases.notDecoded: Line 2, from byte 16, names its field with nothing, or with a character a field name cannot hold - whitespace before its colon is one - so the head is not decoded from it on.

cases.name: a control character in a value
cases.head: request
cases.notDecoded: Line 2, from byte 16, holds a control character in its value, so the head is not decoded from it on.

cases.name: a carriage return ending no line
cases.head: request
cases.notDecoded: Line 2, from byte 16, holds a carriage return that ends no line, so the head is not decoded from it on.

cases.name: a request line with two spaces
cases.head: request
cases.notDecoded: Its first line is not a request line - a method, a target and an HTTP version, one space apart - so nothing is decoded.

cases.name: a method holding a character no token holds
cases.head: request
cases.notDecoded: Its first line is not a request line - a method, a target and an HTTP version, one space apart - so nothing is decoded.

cases.name: a status code of two digits
cases.head: response
cases.notDecoded: Its first line is not a status line - an HTTP version, a three-digit status code and a reason, one space apart - so nothing is decoded.

cases.name: a version that is not HTTP's
cases.head: response
cases.notDecoded: Its first line is not a status line - an HTTP version, a three-digit status code and a reason, one space apart - so nothing is decoded.

cases.name: a head without the empty line that ends it
cases.head: request
cases.notDecoded: The head ends without the empty line that ends a head, so it may have held more fields than those decoded.

cases.name: a head ending inside a line
cases.head: request
cases.notDecoded: The head ends inside line 2, from byte 16, before the empty line that ends a head, so that line is not decoded.

cases.name: a head ending before its first line does
cases.head: request
cases.notDecoded: The head ends before its first line does, so nothing is decoded.

cases.name: the response head WinINet kept of an exchange it made over HTTP/2 (FX-HTTP-006): HTTP/1.1's form, with no reason, its fields named in lower case as HTTP/2 names them

content-type: application/octet-stream
date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 21:44:26 GMT
content-length: 98304
